approach: Extend the one classifier that already exists. In claude.rs add `usage_limit_hit(detail)`, which beside `api_error_status` reads the driver detail `<subtype>: <text>`. It matches only under subtype `success` or `error` (or no prefix), and only when the text starts with "You've hit your weekly/session limit" (case-insensitive, straight or curly apostrophe). It returns the text after "resets" as the reset time. In disk.rs, `producer_stop_reason` and the unprefixed branch of `StopCause::of` treat a 429 or this text as `UsageLimit`. The reason is `environment: usage limit reached: <detail>`, which already contains the reset time. A new `usage_limit_reset(reason)` reads the time back. The producer path in run/producer.rs already routes a usage-limit reason to `self.failure`, and the scope guard already skips environment reasons; neither needs a code change. In drain.rs add `Stop::UsageLimit` (label "usage limit"). In `run_job`, a Failed outcome whose reason is a usage limit sets that stop on the first such job and adds a note `usage limit reached; it resets <time>`. The drain report already prints notes, so display.rs is untouched. Remove UsageLimit from the "failed twice" Environment rule, because the earlier stop makes it unreachable. main.rs gets the help text for the new stop. Tests: a stand-in `claude` script in claude.rs, a classifier test in disk.rs, a run-level test in run/tests.rs, a Stub drain test in tests/drain.rs. CHANGELOG.md gets an entry under Unreleased/Added. Round 2 revision: criterion 6 now states what fails without the behavior and names its seam; the rest of the plan is unchanged.

decisions.choice: Put the text detector next to `api_error_status` in claude.rs as `usage_limit_hit`, and have disk.rs's `producer_stop_reason` and `StopCause::of` call it.
decisions.reason: claude.rs already says 'the driver and the core cannot disagree'. disk.rs is the single classifier read by the scope guard, `athena retry` and the drain. Fixing it there fixes every reader once, which is the root-cause default.

rejected.option: Match the text in producer.rs or in the drain only
rejected.why: That patches one caller. The scope guard would still count the job as a failure and `resumable_stop` would disagree.

rejected.option: Teach `api_error_status` to return Some(429) for the limit text
rejected.why: It would fake an HTTP status the reply never carried, and it would change the 401 retry check in `invoke`.

decisions.choice: Anchor the match at the start of the text, under subtype `success` or `error` or no prefix. Never match under `error_max_turns` or `error_during_execution`, and never mid-prose.
decisions.reason: Same discipline as `api_error_status`. A model's closing words about a limit under another subtype, or a sentence that merely mentions a limit, must stay a work failure (criterion 5).

rejected.why: False positives on prose like 'I fixed the weekly limit handler'.

decisions.choice: Carry the reset time inside the existing reason string and read it back with `disk::usage_limit_reset`. Add no record field and no new record kind.
decisions.reason: The brief forbids a new record kind. `USAGE_LIMIT: <detail>` already holds the whole detail and the closing reason is stored as it is today.

rejected.option: A new field on the job outcome or a new record
rejected.why: Out of scope, and it would touch `check_record_file`, `AnyRecord` and the round-trip test.

decisions.choice: Add `Stop::UsageLimit`, set in `run_job` when a Failed run's reason is `StopCause::UsageLimit`, so the run ends after the first such job. Put the reset time in a `Report.notes` entry `usage limit reached; it resets <time>`.
decisions.reason: The brief asks for a drain stop with reason 'usage limit' and the reset time. Every later item would hit the same limit and a retry wastes a call. display.rs already prints notes after the jobs and `stopped     <label>: <meaning>`, so no display.rs edit is needed.

rejected.option: Reuse `Stop::Environment` after the existing 'fails twice' rule
rejected.why: The label would not be 'usage limit', and a second paid attempt is wasted on a known limit.

rejected.option: Make `Stop::meaning` dynamic to include the reset time
rejected.why: `Stop` is a Copy enum and `display::drain` is not a deliverable. A note is smaller.

decisions.choice: Remove `StopCause::UsageLimit` from the `ItemEnd::Failed` match and narrow the existing drain test `a_usage_limit_or_low_disk_failing_an_item_twice_also_stops_the_batch` (tests/drain.rs:1214) to low disk only.
decisions.reason: The usage-limit stop is set at the first failure, so that arm can never fire first. Keeping it would be two paths for one stop.

rejected.option: Leave the arm in place and keep the old test
rejected.why: The old test would fail because the run now stops on the first failure with a different stop.

decisions.choice: Leave run/producer.rs unchanged and edit run/tests.rs only for tests.
decisions.reason: producer.rs:391-410 calls `producer_stop_reason` on the record detail and sends a `UsageLimit` cause to `self.failure(ctx, &reason)`, keeping nothing. Once `producer_stop_reason` recognises the text the path is correct. No fault there.

rejected.option: Edit the producer comment or flow for the sake of the deliverable
rejected.why: It would add diff with no behavior.

decisions.choice: Criterion 6 is shown by running the three Athena checks together on the whole workspace, naming the tests that break without the behavior.
decisions.reason: The check commands are the criterion; their failure modes without the change are concrete: the help-text test, the Stop::ALL test, the edited drain test, exhaustive matches and -D warnings.

rejected.option: Run only the new tests for criterion 6
rejected.why: That would duplicate criteria 1-5 and not show the workspace-wide checks.

risks.risk: A real limit reply with different wording or subtype is not recognised and stays a work failure.
risks.mitigation: Matching is isolated in one function, `usage_limit_hit`, with tests for weekly and session wording and the curly apostrophe. The existing 429 path is untouched. The wording is recorded as a Host open question.

risks.risk: False positives: a model's own prose that begins with the limit words would be taken as an environment stop.
risks.mitigation: The match is anchored at the start of the text and only under subtype success, error or no prefix; error_max_turns and error_during_execution are excluded, as `api_error_status` already does. The `not_a_usage_limit_*` tests cover this.

risks.risk: The existing test at tests/drain.rs:1214 asserts the old behavior (429 after two failures gives Stop::Environment), so the change breaks it.
risks.mitigation: The plan narrows that test to low disk. A new test covers the 429 reason and the limit text, each ending in Stop::UsageLimit after one run. The change is deliberate: a 429 also stops at the first failure now.

risks.risk: Classifying the limit text as an environment stop makes such jobs resumable by `athena retry` (`resumable_stop` reads StopCause) and uncounted by the scope guard. This could read as a retry or resume change.
risks.mitigation: `resumable_stop`, `keeps_unfinished_work` and `Athena::retry` are not edited. Only the classification input changes, the same as for a 429. The disk.rs test asserts the unchanged outputs for the new reason.

risks.risk: With `[parallel] max_concurrency` above 1, workers already running other items finish their jobs, and a second worker hitting the limit adds a second note.
risks.mitigation: `set_stop` keeps the first reason. Both notes are accurate and no job in flight is killed, which matches the other stop reasons. The drain's job-boundary design is unchanged.

risks.risk: Only the producer stage maps a limit reply to the environment stop; a limit hit in a reader, verifier or planner invocation keeps its current handling.
risks.mitigation: That is the existing 429 scope and the brief says to make no other change. It is listed as a follow-up in the producer's change description.

risks.risk: Adding a Stop variant changes the `--json` output name set.
risks.mitigation: The change is additive (`usage-limit`). A search of the repository found no consumer that matches stop names.

demonstrations.method: New unit tests in `stand_in_tests` of crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs. The STAND_IN script gets modes `weekly_limit` and `session_limit`, each emitting `{"type":"result","subtype":"success","is_error":true,...,"result":"You've hit your weekly limit · resets Nov 12, 3pm"}`. The tests call `driver.invoke` with `counted(dir, "weekly_limit", ..)` as `a_usage_limit_is_not_retried` does, then `usage_limit_hit(&out.detail.unwrap())`.
demonstrations.observes: The outcome is Error and the driver is called once (no 401-style retry). `usage_limit_hit` gives Some with `resets == Some("Nov 12, 3pm")`; the session variant gives the same; a reply with no 'resets' gives Some with `resets == None`.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without `usage_limit_hit` the tests do not compile. A version returning None for these texts fails the Some(..) assertions.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `ClaudeCodeDriver::invoke` and `usage_limit_hit`. The fake is the shell stand-in `claude`, injected through `driver(stand_in(dir), Registry::new(state))` with MODE in `spec.env`. The seam exists (claude.rs:799-861); plan step 2 adds the two modes.

They build the detail with the existing `driver_detail(&result_line("success", "You've hit your weekly limit · resets Nov 12, 3pm"))`, which goes through `StreamState::on_line` and `output_from_result`. Then they call `producer_stop_reason`, `StopCause::of`, `is_environment_reason`, `resumable_stop`, `keeps_unfinished_work` and `usage_limit_reset`, also on the stored unprefixed form `the producer did not complete: <detail>`.
demonstrations.observes: The reason starts with `USAGE_LIMIT` and contains 'resets Nov 12, 3pm'. `StopCause::of` is UsageLimit; `is_environment_reason` is true; `usage_limit_reset` gives Some("Nov 12, 3pm"), None for a bare 429; `resumable_stop(Failed)` is true and `keeps_unfinished_work` false, as for 429 today.

open_questions: Host: The exact text and subtype the real Claude Code CLI emits for a weekly or session limit are not visible in the repository. The plan assumes an is_error result with subtype `success` whose text starts "You've hit your weekly limit · resets <time>", and the tests simulate that. If the live CLI puts the text elsewhere or under another subtype, the detector must be adjusted; a captured real reply would settle it.
